component.name: NEO-M9N Monitor
component.summary: Diagnose and monitor a u-blox NEO-M9N GNSS receiver

description.p: NEO-M9N Monitor tests a SparkFun u-blox NEO-M9N receiver connected directly over USB and shows live GNSS data. It gives explicit evidence for USB and serial failures, loss of fix, frozen navigation epochs, checksum failures and receiver-reported RF or firmware errors.

ul.li: Live fix, position, motion, timing and receiver identity
Sortable satellite table with signal levels and a sky plot
RF, antenna, spoofing and diagnostic freshness indicators
Timed device test with a PASS, WARN or FAIL report
Raw capture, JSONL snapshot and application log evidence files, plus replay
Host diagnostics for USB access, drivers and competing services

description.p: The receiver is only sent read-only diagnostic polls; its configuration is never changed, and passive mode sends nothing at all.

screenshot.caption: Session setup and the live dashboard
Vehicle view: speed, compass, trip and altitude
Map page with an offline map: live position and track

description.p: Coordinate formats: show positions in decimal degrees, degrees and minutes, degrees-minutes-seconds, British National Grid (approximate, ±5 m) or UTM. Logs and exports stay in decimal WGS 84.
Mark position: record where you are as a numbered point with one tap or the M key, see the marks as pins on the map, list, copy, note or delete them, and export them with the track as GPX waypoints.

Clock check: the Host and Receiver pages show how far this computer's clock is from GNSS time, so you know how far to trust log timestamps. Device test reports record it too. The app never changes the clock.
Export Track: save the trip's track as a GPX file for mapping apps, from the Vehicle or Map page or with Ctrl+E. The file is written only where you choose and never sent anywhere.
Night mode: a one-tap dark appearance on the Vehicle and Map pages, and an Appearance menu with Follow System, Light, Dark or Automatic by Sun (dark from dusk to dawn at the receiver's position).
The Dashboard shows sunrise, sunset, day length, civil twilight and the sun's elevation for the receiver's position, calculated locally from GNSS time with no network.

The offline map script keeps its summary on screen: Planetiler's full output goes to a log file and only short progress steps are shown. Running it without an area now says so. A user guide correction.

Adds a Map page: your live position, accuracy and track on a grid, on an offline map file made once at home (works with no internet), or on an OpenStreetMap map you opt into after a privacy notice. The Python package is renamed neo-m9n-monitor.

Adds a Vehicle page for use on the move: a speed gauge, a course-over-ground compass, trip distance, average and maximum speed, moving time and an altitude profile, in large instruments that scale to the window, with km/h or mph and fullscreen.
The command-line interface is replaced by this GTK 4 and libadwaita desktop application.
